findings.title: remove_member uses delete without permission/membership validation and no auth-check for cross-group misuse
findings.body: group.users.delete(user_id) directly removes a user from a group association without verifying the user_id actually belongs to that group or sanitizing it beyond to_i. While not strictly a security hole given admin-only access, the removed code path previously went through group.remove(user) which may trigger model callbacks (e.g., updating is_default_mod_role, etc.) that this new direct ActiveRecord association delete bypasses, potentially leaving related state inconsistent.

findings.title: Route changed from member-scoped id to flat params, breaking existing API consumers
findings.body: The admin groups routes changed from nested resource member actions (which used :id) to collection-level 'members' routes requiring group_id and user_id/usernames params. Any external integrations or other code paths calling the old route structure (e.g. PATCH update for incremental membership changes) will break since update_patch/incremental logic was entirely removed from the controller. This is a breaking API change without any deprecation path mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: members endpoint always paginates now, changing behavior for non-automatic groups
findings.body: Previously, pagination (limit/offset) was only applied for automatic groups; now all groups are always limited to 50 by default. Clients that previously fetched the full member list for small, non-automatic groups in one call now get only 50 members silently unless they also pass offset/limit, which could silently truncate data for existing callers not updated to use pagination.

findings.title: findMembers no longer returns a value usable by old callers expecting a members array
findings.body: findMembers() used to resolve with the array of User objects; now it resolves to undefined and instead mutates the model's own properties (members, user_count, limit, offset) as a side effect. Any remaining caller expecting the promise to resolve with the member list (per the previous contract) will now get undefined, which is a backward-incompatible contract change that could silently break usages outside the files touched in this PR.

findings.title: Template iterates over 'members' but route exposes raw group model without computed property guarantee at render time
findings.body: The route no longer waits for findMembers() to resolve before transitioning (setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning/chaining the promise), so the template may render with 'members' still undefined on first paint, resulting in an empty list rendering before members load asynchronously. This differs from previous behavior where afterModel waited for the promise to resolve before the controller/template were set up, so there's a transient UI flash/empty state regression.
